correctness.rationale: Positive-support independence allows at most one positive vertex in each clique layer. Feasibility forces one in each layer, and cross-layer independence forces distinct matching indices. For n at least three a third index yields, in each layer, a zero vertex with exactly one positive neighbor; its Italian neighborhood sum forces that neighbor to have label two. Every resulting off-matching pair of twos is feasible. The exhaustive checker tests the original definition on all ternary labelings through n=6 and matches the complete classification for every n at least three in that range.

value.rationale: Complete prisms K_n square K_2 are a canonical dense Cartesian-product family. The theorem completely determines every independent Italian function, not just the optimum: all feasible functions have weight four, their supports are exactly the off-matching cross-layer pairs, and there are n(n-1) of them. This exact rigidity gives a natural benchmark for how independent support interacts with Italian defense and is strictly finer than a minimum-only algorithm or bound.
